report.incidentSummary: Starting at approximately 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC) on 2026-10-16, OTP login success dropped from ~97.4% to ~70%, causing approximately one-quarter of user login attempts to fail. Users reported receiving OTP codes that did not work upon entry. Investigation determined that internal dispatch pipelines were healthy: notification-service synchronously handed off all OTP SMS dispatches to sms-provider without errors or elevated latency, message-queue lag and queue depth remained normal, and cache was operating with steady hit rates and no evictions. The root cause is upstream degradation at the external SMS provider and downstream telecom operators, causing over-the-air SMS delivery delays exceeding the 240-second OTP token lifetime (shortened in CHG-48224), resulting in users receiving already-expired OTP codes.
report.rootCauseStatement: Downstream telecom operator routing degradation via the primary external SMS provider caused cellular delivery delays exceeding the 240-second OTP validity window (shortened in CHG-48224 on Oct 14). Because the SMS provider synchronously accepts API dispatches without reporting errors at ingress, internal systems appeared normal while users received expired OTP codes that failed verification in auth-service.

hypotheses.cause: Downstream telecom operator routing degradation at external SMS provider causing over-the-air SMS delivery delays exceeding the 240-second OTP token lifetime
hypotheses.rationale: Internal notification pipeline telemetry (queue lag, notifications queue depth, notification-service p95 latency) and cache health remained completely stable. The SMS provider synchronously accepted all 308 OTP SMS dispatches with no API error spikes. The symptom of users receiving codes that do not work, paired with an abrupt drop from ~97.4% to ~70% at 05:10 UTC, matches past incident PIR-1602 where carrier routing delays caused SMS delivery to arrive past the token validity window (reduced to 240s in CHG-48224).

hypotheses.cause: Infrastructure update CHG-48221 to the auth-service node pool at 04:54 UTC introduced an unobserved runtime or host-level defect on auth-service instances
hypotheses.rationale: Although CHG-48221 upgraded the log shipper agent at 04:54 UTC and broke log ingestion from auth-service, auth-service request rate and p95 latency remained steady at ~297-312 ms across the window, with zero thread deadlock or exhaustion errors. The log shipper upgrade caused an observability dropout rather than functional application degradation.

facts.statement: On 2026-10-14 at 09:30:00 UTC, change CHG-48224 reduced the OTP expiry window in auth-service from 300s to 240s.
On 2026-10-16 at 04:54:00 UTC, infrastructure change CHG-48221 upgraded the log shipper agent from v2.8 to v3.0 on the auth-service node pool.

In auth-service, otp_success_rate remained steady at ~97.4% until 05:05 UTC, then dropped sharply starting at 05:10 UTC to 87.04%, reaching ~71.2% by 05:20 UTC and persisting between 68% and 72% through 07:00 UTC.
In cache, memory_used_pct stayed flat between 61.39% and 62.54%, evictions_per_min remained normal at 31.4 to 42.4 count/min, and cache_hit_rate across all keyspaces remained between 91.9% and 95.7%.

In message-queue, overall queue depth remained between 109.3 and 128.6 messages (notifications queue depth averaged 110.1 messages), and consumer lag remained stable at 1.64s to 2.47s throughout the window.

In notification-service, p95 latency remained flat at ~110.8 to 126.2 ms (mean 119.4 ms), sms_send_failures remained flat at baseline (~3.08 count/min), and 308 OTP SMS messages were logged as synchronously accepted by sms-provider with zero SMS-related errors or timeouts.

In auth-service, logs ceased shipping at 04:54:07.955 UTC following the CHG-48221 log shipper upgrade, but p95 latency remained steady at ~297.3 ms and request rate remained stable at 41 to 46 req/s with a mild increase to 48-52.5 req/s between 05:11 and 05:29 UTC.
Past incident PIR-1602 on 2026-09-09 involved SMS provider downstream operator routing delays of 2 to 5 minutes, which delayed OTP arrival and degraded login completion.

inferences.statement: Internal notification processing and message queuing did not cause delivery delays, as consumer lag, queue depth, notification-service dispatch latency, and SMS API acceptance remained entirely normal.
Cache memory saturation, key evictions, and keyspace misses did not cause OTP verification failures, as cache metrics across all keyspaces operated within healthy nominal ranges.

The cessation of auth-service logs at 04:54:08 UTC was an observability artifact caused by the v3.0 log shipper upgrade rather than application death or thread hang, as request throughput and latency remained healthy.
The slight increase in auth-service traffic between 05:11 and 05:29 UTC was driven by user login retry attempts following validation failures.

The combination of normal SMS dispatch acceptance and users reporting that codes do not work indicates that OTP SMS messages are experiencing downstream telecom delivery delays exceeding the 240-second validity window, rendering delivered OTPs expired upon entry.

assumptions.statement: The external SMS provider is synchronously accepting OTP SMS requests at API ingress but experiencing cellular carrier routing queue delays of greater than 240 seconds for approximately 25% to 30% of user traffic.
auth-service rejects expired OTP tokens with a generic verification failure perceived by end users as 'code not working'.

timeline.event: Config change CHG-48224 applied to auth-service, reducing OTP expiry time from 300s to 240s.
auth-service otp_success_rate healthy at ~97.4%; internal notification queues and cache operating at baseline.

auth-service request rate increases mildly from ~43 req/s to 48-52.5 req/s as users retry failed OTP logins.
notification-service continuously accepts and dispatches OTP SMS messages to sms-provider synchronously (308 OTP messages accepted) without API errors or internal queue delays.

confidence.rationale: High confidence based on comprehensive elimination of all internal failure modes (cache saturation, message queue backlog, notification-service dispatch latency, and auth-service request/latency degradation), combined with precedent in PIR-1602 matching the specific symptom of users receiving codes that arrive expired.
